To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a prolongation of QTc interval increases the risk of cardiovascular disease, 2) QTc interval is associated with cardiovascular risk factors, 3) QTc is associated with blood glucose in women and blood pressure in male young subjects, 4) QT measurement can be useful in the screening of healthy subjects for the prevention of cardiovascular disease.

QT interval prolongation is a predictor of cardiovascular disease in the elderly, but its relationship with cardiovascular risk factors has never been investigated in young subjects; we found that QTc length was associated with blood glucose levels and blood pressure in young healthy subjects; QTc measurement may represent a new tool for the screening of young healthy subjects at risk for cardiovascular disease.
QT interval is prolonged in a percentage of healthy young subjects and that this is associated with cardiovascular risk factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between QT interval and the cardiovascular risk factors in a young healthy population.

the study of the relationship between QT interval and QT dispersion and cardiovascular risk factors (blood pressure, blood glucose, cholesterol, smoking habits and hypertensive familiarity) in a healthy, young population.
the study of the QT interval in healthy young people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the association between the length of the QTc interval, glucose levels, blood pressure and cardiovascular risk factors is present also in healthy young subjects and QT measurement may represent an important tool for the screening of young people for cardiovascular prevention.

the association between QT interval lengthening and cardiovascular risk factors is not a linear phenomenon, but it may be more complicated and influenced by other factors such as gender, age and ethnicity.
QTc prolongation in young subjects may reflect a higher cardiovascular risk, and that QT measurement may be useful as a marker in the screening for cardiovascular prevention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a prolonged QTc interval is present also in healthy young subjects, and it is related to blood pressure and glucose levels.
QT interval is associated with cardiovascular risk factors in young healthy subjects.

the QT interval and the dispersion of the QT interval (QTd) are associated with some cardiovascular risk factors in young healthy subjects and that the QT interval should be considered in the screening for cardiovascular risk factors in the young.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QTc is associated with cardiovascular risk factors in young healthy subjects, and this relationship is present even at very low levels of these risk factors.
the QT interval is a useful marker of risk in young people.
the QT interval is prolonged in a substantial number of healthy young subjects and this prolongation is associated with blood pressure and fasting glucose levels.
